install.short_help: Install tingle onto PATH and enable bash completion.
install.long_help:
Adds tingle's bin/ folder to PATH and installs bash completion for tingle by writing a marked block to ~/.bashrc.

Usage:
    tingle install

Running it more than once is safe: if the block is already present and points at the current tingle folder, ~/.bashrc is left untouched. If the tingle folder has moved since it was installed, re-running tingle install from the new location rewrites the existing block to point at the new path.

Only bash (~/.bashrc) is supported; zsh and fish are not wired up. On macOS, bash login shells read ~/.bash_profile, so make sure it sources ~/.bashrc for the wiring to apply.

To remove the wiring again, run tingle uninstall.

linux.short_help: Run GNU/Linux tools (sed, shell) inside a container.
linux.long_help:
Runs real GNU/Linux command-line tools inside a Docker container (the current working directory mounted in at the same path), for cases where the host tool differs from its Linux counterpart in ways that break scripts or muscle memory — e.g. macOS's BSD sed vs GNU sed.

Usage:
    tingle linux shell [--isolated]
    tingle linux sed <sed-args...>

By default, tingle linux shell brings in host configuration, each item only when it is present on the host: git config (read-only), the SSH agent plus ssh config and known_hosts (read-only; private keys are never mounted), the kubeconfig (read-write; only the first KUBECONFIG path), ~/.aws (read-write), and any non-empty AWS_* variables. git's credential helper is reset inside the container, and on native Linux Docker the container uses host networking. Pass --isolated, or set TINGLE_LINUX_ISOLATED=1, to skip all of this.

Before starting, tingle linux shell prints a one-line banner to stderr with the image version and the bundled tools (marked '(isolated)' when isolated).

Examples:
    tingle linux shell
        Opens an interactive bash shell inside the tingle-linux container,
        with the current working directory mounted at the same path and
        your host git/ssh/kube/aws configuration available, so you can run
        Linux-native tools directly against your files.

    tingle linux shell --isolated
        Opens the same shell without any host configuration: no git, ssh,
        kube or aws config, no SSH agent and no AWS_* variables.
        TINGLE_LINUX_ISOLATED=1 tingle linux shell does the same.

    tingle linux sed -i 's/foo/bar/' somefile.txt
        Runs GNU sed inside the tingle-linux container with all arguments
        forwarded verbatim. Here it edits somefile.txt in place using GNU
        -i syntax (no backup-suffix argument, unlike BSD sed).

    cat file | tingle linux sed 's/a/b/'
        Pipes stdin through GNU sed inside the container and writes the
        result to stdout.

See docs/guides/linux.md for the full tool list and known limitations.

uninstall.short_help: Remove tingle's PATH and bash completion wiring from ~/.bashrc.
uninstall.long_help:
Removes the tingle block (the lines between '# >>> tingle >>>' and '# <<< tingle <<<') that tingle install added to ~/.bashrc. The rest of ~/.bashrc is left untouched.

Usage:
    tingle uninstall

The tingle folder itself is not deleted; remove it manually if you no longer need it. Running it more than once is safe: if no tingle block is found, nothing is changed. Restart your shell afterwards to drop tingle from PATH.

update.short_help: Update a web install of tingle to the latest or a pinned release.
update.long_help:
Updates a web install of tingle (one with a tingle.json file) to the latest release, or to a pinned one. It always updates the folder of the tingle being run, and names that folder in its output.

Usage:
    tingle update [--check] [--force] [<version>]

Without a version, the target is the latest stable GitHub release (pre-releases and drafts are skipped). When the installed version already matches it, tingle prints 'tingle is already up to date (<version>)' and changes nothing.

Pass <version>, or set TINGLE_VERSION, to pin the target. It must be X.Y.Z or X.Y.Z-<suffix> (no 'v' prefix) and 0.4.0 or later; older versions are refused with 'tingle update can only install 0.4.0 or later'. A pin may be older than the installed version (a downgrade) and may be a pre-release. When both are given, the argument wins over TINGLE_VERSION.

Options:
    --check    Dry run: print the installed and target versions and, when the
               install tracks file hashes, the shipped files you edited
               locally. Exits 0 without downloading or changing anything.
    --force    Update even when shipped files were edited locally; those
               edits are overwritten.

Before changing anything, tingle update asks for confirmation (y/N). Set TINGLE_ASSUME_YES (to any value) to skip the prompt; without a terminal it is required. The release zip is verified against its SHA-256 checksum before anything is replaced. Files you added to the tingle folder are kept.

A git checkout of tingle is not updated by this command: it prints a message saying to update it with git pull instead, and exits non-zero.

See docs/guides/update.md for more details.
